It involves analyzing energy usage data, implementing energy-saving strategies and technologies, and evaluating the results to continuously improve energy performance. The ultimate goals are to achieve greater energy efficiency, save money, and promote reliability. 8 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2.3.1 Energi-zing! 2.3.1.1 Objective Develop a solution to improve energy usage in U.S. buildings (residential, commercial, new, or existing). Student team solutions should lead to reductions in energy use, and students should emphasize reducing barriers to obtaining technologies. 2.3.1.2 Background Demand for electricity is growing across the residential and commercial buildings space because of increases in the built infrastructure, plug-in vehicles, appliances, plug loads (televisions, video games, IoT devices), and electrically powered space conditioning. As demand grows, so will the requirement for market transformation across multiple sectors, including power generation and storage options, increased energy efficiency adoption, and timely use of energy across homes and places of work. New infrastructure will be needed to support these technologies, and managing electricity usage in buildings will play an integral role in achieving these objectives. Electricity use in buildings has increased threefold to fivefold between 1970 and 2020, with space conditioning equipment and plug loads accounting for the largest shares (U.S. EIA 2023). These realities provide opportunities to improve energy management strategies, adopt energy- efficient technologies, and implement other efforts that can address energy challenges. However, there are key barriers that impact improvements. Consider that almost half of the U.S. housing stock was built before 1970 (Sarkar 2011). Unless a home has had a substantial infrastructure upgrade, most of these homes have electrical breaker panels with 100-amp service or less. The average cost to upgrade a home to 200-amp service ranges from $1,300–$2,500, not to mention additional constraints and implications from charging electric vehicles (The Home Guide 2022; Thiele 2022). Meeting the electricity demand of contemporary buildings while balancing technical and capital constraints will require innovative solutions. Such a substantial transformation across the residential and commercial building sectors will also depend on widespread adoption of new and existing technologies. 2.3.1.3 Challenge Develop an innovative solution that will address energy use in buildings. Solutions can be considered at the individual building and multibuilding scale. Teams should first develop a focused problem statement for a specific stakeholder group and then develop a technical solution or process to solve the chosen problem. Suggestions for student teams include (but are not limited to) the following: • Develop solutions (equipment, technologies, or processes) to address the limited electrical infrastructure in individual buildings, communities, or regions. • Improve existing equipment or technologies to significantly increase capabilities. • Develop technologies or processes to identify optimal combinations of high-performance HVAC equipment and building envelope system upgrades. •
